notes: Requirement-level labels. 'expected' is the verdict a careful human reviewer would give from the code; 'acceptable' lists verdicts that are defensible given static evidence only (no deployment). Evidence cites the files read while labelling.

requirements.evidence: frontend RequestForm -> POST /api/generate (webapp/server.py) -> service.generate_from_form builds document pipeline with 5 generators (brd_agent_suite/pipeline.py)
auto_fields passed from the form to generate_from_form and into gap_filler_agent state; enrichment itself is LLM-driven
normalize_form forces excluded fields empty; NEVER_EXCLUDABLE_FIELDS backstop (webapp/service.py); section omission in documents relies on generator prompts
additional_sections is a FORM_FIELDS list_obj passed through to requirements JSON; rendering into documents is prompt-driven
POST /api/runs/{run_id}/export/{doc} -> service.export_docx runs pandoc on markdown that references architecture.png/flowchart.png uploaded via /diagrams
service.revise_run creates a new run id with parent_run_id and never overwrites the original run directory
build_document_pipeline: SequentialAgent [first stage, ParallelAgent(5 generators), consistency_check_agent]
ResultsView renders documents and Mermaid diagrams in tabs via DocumentRenderer; 'side-by-side' layout not evident - tabbed previews
Generators run in a ParallelAgent (design supports speed); a 90 s threshold cannot be proven without running it
load_dotenv in webapp/server.py; frontend only calls /api/* on the backend; no key in frontend code
No retry logic anywhere (grep retry/backoff: none). Errors are logged (observability.log_model_error_call) and surfaced as HTTP 500 detail - reporting yes, retry no
marked and mermaid are npm dependencies bundled by Next.js (frontend/package.json, lib/mermaidSetup.ts); no CDN references found
